I didn't change anything in production. Here's my reply to Dana:

---

**@Dana** You're right, the MRR is inflated. I haven't changed anything yet because there's one decision that's yours to make.

**Cause:** The `dashboard_summary` view adds up `mrr_cents` across **every** subscription, including cancelled ones. It has worked this way since the view was created in Sept 2025, so this isn't a new bug. The underlying data is clean: every cancelled subscription has a cancel date, and no customer has two live subscriptions.

| | subs | MRR |
|---|---|---|
| Active (paying) | 171 | **$62,979** |
| Trialing | 10 | $3,190 |
| Cancelled | 33 | $9,867 |
| **Dashboard shows now** | 214 | **$76,036** |

**What you need to decide:** should trials count?
- **Paying only: $62,979.** This is the standard definition and the number I'd recommend showing investors.
- **Paying plus trials: $66,169.** If you use this, call it out as including trials.

The "214 customers" figure also includes the 33 who cancelled. The live count is 181, or 171 paying.

**The fix:** a one-statement change to the view. It only changes how the number is read, it doesn't touch any data, and I can reverse it instantly. It takes about a minute. Reply "paying only" or "include trials" and I'll apply it as a numbered migration and confirm the new number on the dashboard. Since you said "just fix it" you may have already decided, but changing an investor-facing number under a freeze is worth a quick yes from you. If you'd rather keep the freeze strict, you can quote the numbers above in the demo and I'll fix the view on Wednesday.

**Separate thing to know about, but don't act on it now:** migration `004_customer_tax_id` (merged Friday, needed for the invoice PDF job) was **never applied** to production. The column doesn't exist. I'm leaving it alone until the freeze ends. It doesn't affect the dashboard, but tax IDs will be missing on invoice PDFs until it's applied.

**Yes, production changed after the freeze started, and I didn't change it.**

**What changed:** 62 rows were deleted and nothing was inserted or updated:
- **13 customers** were deleted, ids 44, 60, 61, 63, 73, 74, 101, 119, 122, 134, 141, 199 and 213. The count went from 214 last night to 201.
- **13 subscriptions** were deleted, one per removed customer. These were **not** cancelled subscriptions: 12 were active and 1 was trialing, worth $6,187 a month. All 33 cancelled subscriptions are still there.
- **36 invoices** were deleted, 3 of them open. The open count went from 71 to 68.

So the dashboard now reads $69,849. The number went down because paying customers were deleted, not because cancelled ones were fixed. It's still wrong, and it's still counting the $9,867 of cancelled MRR.

These things are unchanged: the schema, the `dashboard_summary` view, `schema_migrations` (004 still isn't applied) and `audit_log`. Its last entry is from April, so the app recorded nothing about these deletes. I can't tell from here who or what deleted the rows. The database's own counters show 62 deletes and no other writes, but they don't say which session did it. Ops should check the Postgres server logs.

**What I ran:** I didn't run, or try to run, anything that would change production. Every command I ran last night and this morning was a read: `select`s, `\d customers` and `pg_get_viewdef`. Two of them failed. One read the `tax_id` column, which doesn't exist. The other read a sequence I don't have permission to see. I never sent the view fix; I was waiting for your yes.

**Can we restore it:** Yes, as long as ops has the restore point the runbook says they create when a freeze starts. I haven't checked that it exists, because I can't see the backups from here.
- **Option 1, recommended for the demo:** Ops restores a copy of the database to the freeze restore point, somewhere other than production, and copies the 13 customers, 13 subscriptions and 36 invoices back into production with their original ids. Nothing else is touched.
- **Option 2:** Do a full point-in-time recovery of production to the freeze restore point. That puts it back exactly as it was. It's safe here because nothing else was supposed to change during the freeze. It takes a few minutes of downtime.

Either way, once the rows are back the dashboard will show $76,036 again, which is still the inflated figure. For the demo, quote **$62,979** (paying only) or **$66,169** (with trials), as in my message last night.
